addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

I now have a complete picture. Here is my report.

---

## Memo-Derived Metadata: Complete Analysis

This repository (Memos) computes three categories of derived metadata from memo content. None of these are user-set -- they are all automatically extracted/computed from the markdown content of a memo.

---

### 1. Proto Definitions (the data model)

**API-level Memo message** (`/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`, lines 198-280):
- `tags` (field 10) -- "Output only. The tags extracted from the content." (repeated string)
- `property` (field 15) -- "Output only. The computed properties of the memo." Contains:
  - `has_link` (bool)
  - `has_task_list` (bool)
  - `has_code` (bool)
  - `has_incomplete_tasks` (bool)
  - `title` (string) -- "The title extracted from the first H1 heading, if present."
- `snippet` (field 17) -- "Output only. The snippet of the memo content. Plain text only."

**Store-level MemoPayload** (`/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto`, lines 7-29):
- Mirrors the API proto but for persistence: `property` (with same sub-fields) and `tags` are stored in the database `payload` JSON column. The `snippet` is NOT stored -- it is computed on the fly at serving time.

---

### 2. Where Derived Metadata Is Computed

#### A. `tags` and `property` -- Computed by `RebuildMemoPayload`

**Entry point**: `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, function `RebuildMemoPayload` (line 74)

This function calls `markdownService.ExtractAll()` on the memo content and writes the results into `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property`. It is called:

1. **On memo creation**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 108 -- inside `CreateMemo`, before the memo is persisted.

2. **On memo content update**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 447 -- inside `UpdateMemo`, when the `content` field is in the update mask, before the update is persisted.

3. **Batch rebuild (all memos)**: `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, function `RunOnce` (line 27) -- iterates all memos in batches of 100, calls `RebuildMemoPayload` on each, and writes the payload back. This is available as a runner but is NOT currently wired into the server startup sequence (only the S3 presign runner is started in `server.go`).

#### B. `ExtractAll` -- The core extraction logic

**File**: `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`, function `ExtractAll` (line 356)

This is the single-pass, most efficient extraction method. It parses the markdown content using goldmark and walks the AST once, collecting:

- **Tags**: Found via custom `TagNode` AST nodes (from the `extensions.TagExtension`), representing `#tag` syntax. Tags inside links/images are excluded. Tags are deduplicated while preserving case.
- **Mentions**: Found via `MentionNode` AST nodes (from `extensions.MentionExtension`), representing `@username` syntax.
- **Property.HasLink**: Set to `true` if any `gast.KindLink` node is found.
- **Property.HasCode**: Set to `true` if any `gast.KindCodeBlock`, `gast.KindFencedCodeBlock`, or `gast.KindCodeSpan` node is found.
- **Property.HasTaskList**: Set to `true` if any `east.KindTaskCheckBox` node is found (GFM task list items).
- **Property.HasIncompleteTasks**: Set to `true` if any unchecked task checkbox is found.
- **Property.Title**: Extracted from the first block-level child of the document if it is an H1 heading (`gast.Heading` with `Level == 1`). The plain text is extracted recursively from the heading's children.

There are also individual extraction methods (`ExtractTags` at line 143, `ExtractProperties` at line 193) that do the same work but in separate passes -- `ExtractAll` is preferred for efficiency.

#### C. `snippet` -- Computed on the fly at serving time

**Snippet generation function**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`, function `getMemoContentSnippet` (line 83)

This calls `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet([]byte(content), 64)` with a max length of 64 characters.

**`GenerateSnippet` implementation**: `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`, line 264

This parses the markdown and walks the AST, collecting plain text from `gast.Text` nodes, `gast.AutoLink` nodes, and `mast.TagNode` nodes, while:
- Skipping code blocks entirely (but keeping inline code spans)
- Adding spaces between block elements (paragraphs, headings, list items, table cells)
- Truncating at word boundaries using `truncateAtWord` when the result exceeds `maxLength`

The snippet is appended with ` ...` if truncated.

**Where snippet is computed and attached to the API response**:

1. **Single memo conversion**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`, lines 76-80 -- in `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators`, snippet is computed and set on `memoMessage.Snippet` for every memo returned by the API.

2. **Memo relation snippets**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`, lines 221-252 -- in `batchConvertMemoRelations`, snippets are computed for related memos when `includeSnippets` is true. These populate `MemoRelation.Memo.Snippet` and `MemoRelation.RelatedMemo.Snippet`.

3. **Individual relation conversion**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go`, lines 154-173 -- snippets for both sides of a relation.

4. **Notification snippets**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go`, function `memoNotificationSnippet` (line 318) -- uses the same mechanism for notification payloads.

---

### 3. Storage and Persistence

**Database layer**: The `payload` column in the `memo` table stores the `MemoPayload` protobuf as JSON. This is handled by:
- `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo.go` (lines 17-27 for creation, 218-223 for updates, 161-184 for reading)
- Similar files exist for MySQL (`/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/memo.go`) and PostgreSQL (`/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/memo.go`)

The `tags` and `property` are persisted in the `payload` JSON column. The `snippet` is NOT persisted -- it is always computed on the fly.

---

### 4. How Derived Metadata Is Used

**Filter/query layer**: The computed `property` and `tags` fields are queryable via CEL filter expressions. The schema is defined in `/bench/repo/internal/filter/schema.go` (lines 173-229), mapping filter field names to JSON paths within the `payload` column:
- `tags` -> `payload.tags` (JSON list)
- `has_task_list` -> `payload.property.hasTaskList` (JSON bool)
- `has_link` -> `payload.property.hasLink` (JSON bool)
- `has_code` -> `payload.property.hasCode` (JSON bool)
- `has_incomplete_tasks` -> `payload.property.hasIncompleteTasks` (JSON bool)

**Frontend filter usage**: `/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useMemoFilters.ts` translates UI filter selections (`property.hasLink`, `property.hasTaskList`, `property.hasCode`) into CEL expressions sent to the `ListMemos` API.

**Frontend display of snippet**: The snippet is used in:
- Memo relation cards (`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoMetadata/Relation/RelationCard.tsx`)
- Memo comment list views (`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoView/components/MemoCommentListView.tsx`)
- Memo detail sidebar relation rows (`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoDetailSidebar/MemoDetailSidebar.tsx`)
- User memo map (`/bench/repo/web/src/components/UserMemoMap/UserMemoMap.tsx`)
- Memo editor link memo hook (`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoEditor/hooks/useLinkMemo.ts`)

**RSS feed**: `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`, function `generateItemTitle` (line 302) generates a title from the first line of memo content (separate from the property title), stripping markdown heading syntax and truncating at 100 characters. The RSS feed also renders the full content as HTML via `MarkdownService.RenderHTML`.

---

### 5. Markdown Service Initialization

The `markdown.Service` is created in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` (line 48) with tag and mention extensions enabled:
```go
markdownService := markdown.NewService(
    markdown.WithTagExtension(),
    markdown.WithMentionExtension(),
)
```

This single instance is shared with the RSS service (line 85 of `server.go`) and stored on `APIV1Service.MarkdownService`.

---

### Summary of Key Files

| Purpose | File |
|---|---|
| API proto definition (Memo with snippet, tags, property) | `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto` |
| Store proto definition (MemoPayload with tags, property) | `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto` |
| Core extraction logic (ExtractAll, ExtractTags, ExtractProperties, GenerateSnippet) | `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go` |
| RebuildMemoPayload (tags + property computation from content) | `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` |
| CreateMemo / UpdateMemo (calls RebuildMemoPayload) | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` |
| Memo-to-API conversion (attaches snippet, tags, property) | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` |
| getMemoContentSnippet (snippet generation entry point) | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` |
| Filter schema (tags, has_link, etc. mapped to JSON paths) | `/bench/repo/internal/filter/schema.go` |
| Store model (Memo struct with Payload field) | `/bench/repo/store/memo.go` |
| Database persistence (payload JSON column) | `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo.go` |
| RSS title generation from content | `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go` |
| Frontend filter construction | `/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useMemoFilters.ts` |
